title: Florida House, District 58
what_it_does: Represents District 58 (Part of Pinellas) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Kimberly Berfield
candidates.occupation: State representative for District 58; former health-care executive (Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital, WellCare) and former deputy secretary, Florida Department of Health
candidates.background: Qualified for the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot according to the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list (Qualified). Not yet researched.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted yes on HJR 1-F in the June 2026 special session, which placed Amendment 3 on the November ballot to raise the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 and to limit how counties and cities may spend property-tax revenue. Her campaign website names addressing skyrocketing property taxes as a top goal.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HJR 1F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), passage 75-26
Kimberly Berfield for Florida House (campaign website)

immigration.summary: Voted yes on SB 2-C (2025), which created the State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state help with federal detainers, barred driver licenses for unauthorized immigrants, and funded an Unauthorized Alien Transport Program.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), passage 85-30

abortion.summary: Voted yes on SB 300 (2023), the law that limits most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, SB 300 (Heartbeat Protection Act, six-week abortion limit), passage 70-40

guns.summary: Voted yes on HB 543 (2023), which allows carrying a concealed firearm without a state license.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/HB 543 (concealed carry without a license), passage 76-32

education_choice.summary: Voted yes on HB 1 (2023), which removed income limits and enrollment caps so state scholarship funds can follow any K-12 student to private or home education. Her website says families should be able to pursue education for their children in the best environment for each child.

sources.title: Florida House roll-call vote, CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1 (universal school-choice scholarships), passage 83-27
Kimberly Berfield - The Issues (campaign website)

taxes.summary: Her issues page says lower taxes and responsible government spending are critical, and she supports cutting the business rent tax.
taxes.quote: Lower taxes and responsible government spending are critical to ensure our economy thrives.

sources.title: Kimberly Berfield - The Issues (campaign website)
